plain.description: What this regime's legal status means today, in calm plain words, grounded in the source the regime cites (for a court order, the order itself). Shown wherever an item depends on the regime.

derivation.description: verbatim: the value is written in the quoted words. reading: Duly derived the value from the quoted words; the note says how.

plain.description: The rule in plain words for an average student: what the rule says, in general terms, never about a person and never an instruction. Written from the quote by the content lane, checked by tools.sources.plain, and shown first; the exact words stay one tap away.

plain_terms.description: The quote's terms of art that the plain words must keep word for word (for example "U.S. worker", "period of admission", "post-completion academic training"). Each is found in the quote and in the plain words; checked by tools.sources.plain. An empty list says the quote has none.

effective_from_basis.description: stated: the source names the day the rule took effect. earliest_saved_copy: the day is only the date of the oldest saved copy, and the rule may be older. An event before such a day is never called earlier than the rule.

path.description: The category's path as data. The engine reads it and holds no scenario of its own.

counters.description: Counts that need more than date arithmetic. Each names one of four calculators in the engine, its scope and its limit rule

records.description: The kinds of record a case may hold for this category, and their fields

checks.description: Tests on the person's own dates and answers. Each works as a conflict or a judgement item

checklists.description: Ordered steps an official source lists for a stage, as pack data. Each step names its rules, and the output reads its confirmation from confirmations under step.<checklist id>.<step id>

watch.description: The dates on the person's records that run out and are worth watching, such as a card's end. The output lists each as a watch item for every record of the kind that holds the date

checkins.description: The records whose facts go stale and are asked again. The output lists a check-in for each record of the kind, due a product setting's days after the last confirmed day

quote.description: Exact words from the source that support the value.

snapshot.description: Saved copy of the source, relative to the pack folder.

setting.description: The id of a product setting in contracts/product_settings.yaml, in place of a rule. Allowed only in the opens or closes of a stage's window: the window it dates is then a planning window, marked planning in the output, and never shown as law. This schema shares the amount shape with every date, so the pack loader (engine/rulepack.py) refuses a setting anywhere else (W2-P1). Its unit comes from the setting

amount.description: A rule's value, or in a window's dates a product setting's value, added or taken away. Exactly one of rule and setting. Its unit (days, business_days, months) comes from the rule or the setting. A literal number is never allowed: every amount is a sourced rule or a named product setting.

when.description: A date: a fact the person entered, the end of a span or the close of a window already computed, or today, moved by rule amounts. Nothing else. fact may be a fact id, a path over records (this.<field>, following at most two links, as in this.program.end_date), or today, the person's calendar day.

window_opens.description: The open day of a window already computed, by window id. Refused at pack load until the engine works it (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 11)

window_closes.description: The close day of a window already computed, by window id. Refused at pack load until the engine works it (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 11)

month_day_rule.description: A rule holding MM-DD, placed in the year of the fact named by in_year_of

optional.description: Inside earliest_of or latest_of: passed over only when its value is known to be none. An optional member that is unknown, or whose rule is not in force on the day it is read for, makes the whole date unknown and keeps its gaps; it is never read as no cut-off. A member that is not optional and is none makes the date none: the output does not apply. A member that is not yet takes part as the condition's ordering says (in latest_of it is later than every day up to today) (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 16)

as_of.description: Read `fact`, a field with history, as it stood on this day. When this day is unknown, the read is unknown, unless no change record could apply to that field of that record, in which case the value is the same on every day and is known; no change record could apply only when the change kind is stated whole. When this day is not yet (the event has not happened), the value as it stands today. Never today in place of an unknown day (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 26)

in_fiscal_year_of.description: With month_day_rule: the month and day inside the fiscal year that holds this fact's date

fiscal_year_rule.description: A rule holding MM-DD, the first day of a fiscal year

day_before.description: The calendar day before. Not an amount

day_after.description: The calendar day after. Not an amount

first.description: The earliest or latest known value of a date field over the decided records a selector chooses. A chosen record whose date is none is passed over; one whose date is not yet is ordered after every day up to today and compared with later days as the condition says. A record that is undecided, or chosen with an unknown date, leaves the found value standing only when its date is known and cannot beat it (not before it for earliest, not after it for latest); otherwise the result is unknown with its gaps. A found value also needs the list stated whole, since a record not entered could beat it. Nothing chosen: none when no record is undecided and the list is stated whole, else unknown (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN points 14 and 15)

label.description: What the person is asked, in plain words

happened.description: A date of something that already took place, such as a filing. It may not be after today.

school.description: The value depends on the person's school.

rule_ids.description: The rules behind the window. For a planning window, the rules of the step it prepares for; the setting itself is never a rule

done_when.description: Facts that record the step as taken. Once any is entered, the window no longer matters and is not shown as ahead.

entered_when.description: Facts that, all entered, place the person in this stage

ends_also.description: Other sources for the same end. When one gives a different day, both are shown, the items that use the end are null, and the judgement item <stage id>.end_by_source.<record id> is raised

follows.description: Stages this one comes after. The engine checks each for a gap or an overlap the rules do not allow. Refused at pack load until the engine works it (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 11)

gap_allowed.description: The gap the rules allow between this stage and one it follows. Refused at pack load until the engine works it (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 11)

next.description: Stages that can follow. Their windows are computed and shown as what comes next

only_if.description: Conditions under which the list applies to this stage. Refused at pack load until the engine works it (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 11)

rule_ids.description: The rules that define the stage itself

for_each.description: The stage is entered once for each record the selector finds. Its instance id is <stage id>.<record id>, and every item, question and conflict it raises ends with the record id

checklist.description: The id of the checklist in path.checklists that lists this stage's steps

grows_with_time.description: A statement that the list is whole covers only the days through its day

complete_label.description: The question that asks whether the list is whole

label.description: What the person is asked, in plain words

not_sure.description: not_sure is an answer to this choice

to.description: For a link: the record kinds it may name

translation_only.description: Filled only by the translation of an older case. No form asks for it

when_absent.description: What this field left out or null means (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 2). ask, the default: absence is unknown and is asked. not_yet: the event has happened on no day up to and including today (a job's end, a return from a trip, a filing); read as the known value not yet, never as none, and listed among an item's inputs as not yet. none: there is none (an outcome not yet given, a job that is not on campus); read as the known value none, listed as none. An object makes absence depend on this record (point 2a). The screen words the empty field from this declaration, so leaving it empty is the person's statement, not a guess. The values an unknown could take are, for ask and none, every readable value and none, and for not_yet, every readable value and not yet

document.description: K7 (SPEC-W2 point 44a, N7, D97(1)): the document this field is typed from. The engine asks one confirmation per record and document kind for the typed fields that name it, never one per date. A field with no document (a job's start) is asked once with its record.

not_yet.description: Conditions that, all true, make absence the known value not yet. Read first

none.description: Conditions that, all true, make absence the known value none. Read after not_yet

else.description: What absence means when every list is false

absence_by_record.description: Absence that depends on the record (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN point 2a), such as a card's dates that are not yet while no decision has come. Each list of conditions reads this record's own fields only (this.<field>). The lists are read in the order not_yet, then none: the first list that is true gives the state, and else applies when every list is false. When a list is unknown before any is true, absence is unknown, and both the condition's gaps and this field's absent gap are asked. A condition may not read a field whose own when_absent is an object: refused at pack load (point 11)

record.description: The record kind that changes this field

link.description: Its field naming the record changed

from.description: Its date field from which the new value holds

order.description: One field's choices from lowest to highest. A comparison with a value not listed is unknown

selector.description: Records whose conditions are true are chosen; records with an unknown condition are undecided and asked; a decided record is never dropped for an undecided one. A record with a false condition is left out. Inside, this is the record tested and outer is the record of the stage, check or counter that uses the selector. While the kind's list is not stated whole, a record not entered could still be chosen (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN points 13 and 14)

field.description: The path the test reads. With no operator: a flag gives its value (false is false); a field of any other kind reads as present: true

condition.description: One test, true, false or unknown (SPEC-W2-UNKNOWN points 6 to 8). A value read is known (K), the known value none (N) or not yet (Y) that a field's when_absent gives, or unknown (U): absent on a field whose when_absent is ask, unreadable against its kind, or not_sure. A path through a link that is N or Y gives N; through a link that is U it gives U, naming the link. A test is true or false only when every value the unknowns could take gives that same answer. By operator. Field alone: a flag gives its value (false is false); any other kind as present: true. present true or false: K gives true or false; N or Y gives false or true; U gives U and is asked. in: K tests membership; N or Y false; U unknown. on_or_before, on_or_after, before, after: both sides K are compared; Y is later than a known day on or before today, and against a known day after today the test is unknown with a pending gap, not asked; either side N false; else either side U unknown. level_above, level_same, level_below: both sides K and ranked are compared; N or Y false; U unknown. same_as, differs_from: both sides K are compared; either side N or Y false (a join on nothing is no join; for both none use present: false); else either side U unknown. month_day_is: K compared; N or Y false; U unknown. at_most: a K number compared with the rule value; N or Y false; U unknown. exists: true if a decided record is chosen; false if no record is chosen, none is undecided and the list is stated whole; else unknown. none: the negation of exists. count_below n, with k chosen and u undecided: false if k is n or more; true if the list is stated whole and k + u is below n; else unknown. count_at_most n: false if k is above n; true if the list is stated whole and k + u is n or less; else unknown. all_of: false if any is false; true if all are true; else unknown. any_of: true if any is true; false if all are false; else unknown. not: true and false swap; unknown stays unknown. A list of conditions reads as all_of. A test settled by one member asks nothing for the others; a test that is unknown asks every gap it rests on. Amounts are rules, never literal numbers

only_if.description: All true: shown. Any false: not shown. Otherwise shown with the line that the question is for the DSO, and what is missing is asked

bind.description: Fields of the record not yet entered that the next stage is computed for, each from a path of this one, such as program: outer.id

check.description: False: a conflict asks whether these are the dates on the person's documents, and a yes gives talk_to_dso; a judgement gives talk_to_dso at once. Unknown: what is missing is asked

chain_link.description: For chain: the field by which a later record names the first

value_of.description: For same_value: the path whose value groups the records, such as this.program.level

span.description: For sum_of_days and sum_of_months, each record's span. For days_without_qualifying_period, each group's counting window

not_qualifying.description: Records whose days are counted even when a qualifying record covers them

reading.description: True when the checklist is Duly's assembly of several rules into one list, not one source's own list. The screen marks it as Duly's reading

label.description: What the source lists, in plain general words. Never an instruction and never about a person

rule_ids.description: The rules behind the step, at least one of them from a primary source

who.description: Whom the source names for the step

school.description: The step depends on the person's school

record.description: The record kind in path.records that holds the date

field.description: Its date field to watch, as the person typed it from the document

label.description: What the date is, in plain general words, never about a person

rule_ids.description: The rules that make the date matter

watch.description: One date to watch. The record's own date is shown; when it is near is a product setting, never a rule

record.description: The record kind in path.records whose facts are asked again

field.description: Its date field holding the last day the person confirmed the record, such as confirmed_on

setting.description: The id of the product setting in contracts/product_settings.yaml that gives how long a confirmation holds before it is asked again. A setting, never a rule

checkin.description: One kind of record checked in on. Counts that read the record stop at the last confirmed day

document_kind.description: A document kind, the same list as contracts/desktop_documents_bridge.schema.json $defs.kind (a test keeps the two equal).

when.description: Conditions over this record's own fields (this.<field>), all true.

else.description: The kind when no case is true; null means the field is typed from no document there.

document_by_record.description: A document kind that depends on the record, read like absence_by_record: the cases in order, the first whose conditions are all true names the kind. For example an authorization's card_start is typed from the EAD card on OPT and from the Form I-20 for CPT.
